sentences.text: Dated this the 17th day of January, 2024  ORDER
Petitioners have invoked the jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C to quash all proceedings against them.

2. Petitioners are accused Nos. 1 and 2 in L.P.C.No.167/2023 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Thaliparamba arising out of Crime No.61/2021 of Kudiyanmala Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Thaliparamba
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The 2 nd respondent is the defacto complainant.

3. According to the prosecution, accused cheated the de facto complainant of an amount of Rs.7,75,000/- in the year 2019 after promising to secure a job in Israel for the de facto complainant's wife, and thereafter failed to secure a job abroad or return the money, and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for the respondent, apart from the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the matter has been settled and hence the proceedings against the petitioners ought to be quashed.
It was also submitted that, considering the nature of offences alleged, no purpose would be served by continuing the proceedings.

6. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303], the Apex Court has held that in appropriate cases, the High Court can take note of the amicable resolution of disputes between the victim and the wrongdoer to put an end to the criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This view was reiterated in Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [(2014) 6 SCC 466] and Yogendra Yadav and Others v. State of Jharkhand and Another [(2014) 9 SCC 653].
7.

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [(2014) 6 SCC 466]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Yogendra Yadav and Others v. State of Jharkhand and Another [(2014) 9 SCC 653]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have perused Annexure-C affidavit filed by the 2 nd respondent.
The learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that upon verification, it is understood that the affidavit is genuine, and the de facto complainant stands by the contents thereof.
I am satisfied that the matter has been settled and no public interest is involved in this case.
There is no impediment for granting the prayer for quashing.
The continuance of the proceedings will only be an exercise in futility.

8. Though the first accused is presently residing abroad and the case has been transferred to the long pending register, considering the circumstances that the crime was registered on the basis of a private complaint and the parties have settled the dispute among themselves, I am of the view that a Ranjini Akhilesh vs State Of Kerala on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51929229/
2 lenient view can be adopted.
